note: Facts Saathi may speak about leaving, overstaying and getting home. Every fact carries a source, the date it was read, and a status. confirmed = the official page was opened and the figure read on it. official_headline = only the headline of an official page was read. official_snippet = an official page was found by search but not opened. Saathi speaks confirmed facts with 'according to the official website, check with the embassy'; it never speaks anything else as fact. Re-check every entry before launch.

overstay_fine_per_day.note: The page states no grace period. An older government fee page listed other rates; do not mention a grace period.

extension.note: The page gives no filing deadline and does not say who must apply.

departure_permit.note: A ticket with a departure date within 7 days is required; a fine of AED 50 a day starts from the eighth day after the permit expires.

no_passport.eligible: Indian citizen with no valid travel document, or an illegal resident
documents: previous passport (copy or details) or another photo ID
no_passport.note: A total of AED 87 including other charges appears in a search snippet but not on this page: do not say it.

labour.passport_withholding: Official guidance says confiscating a worker's passport is prohibited and workers need no permission to leave; MoHRE says domestic workers may keep their own documents, so the rule differs by worker category.

overstay_penalty.note: Only the headline was read: fine up to SAR 50,000, imprisonment and deportation. The length of imprisonment, any per-day fine and any entry ban are NOT confirmed: never quote a total.

labour.note: The official page describes a general contact centre (Sunday to Thursday, 8 AM to 5 PM). It does not say the line takes labour complaints: do not call it a complaint line.

not_verified: who must file a UAE visit-visa extension and by when
never: promise a return date or that the embassy will pay
claim an amnesty or grace period
advise working on a visit visa
tell the worker to hide or run
